uncited: Chunk-based spatial partitioning divides a volumetric dataset into fixed-size spatial subvolumes (chunks or bricks) to manage memory, enable out-of-core streaming, and facilitate parallel processing [Parent].
It solves the problem of handling datasets larger than available main memory or GPU VRAM by ensuring only relevant chunks reside in active memory [2369-chunk-based-world-streaming.md].

It is distinguished from sibling methods by its reliance on fixed-size spatial blocks as the atomic unit of data management, contrasting with [Sectioning](1636-sectioning.md)'s view-dependent slicing, [Uniform Block Partitioning with Acceleration](6098-uniform-block-partitioning-with-acceleration.md)'s focus on local acceleration within a single context, and [Distributed computing and load balancing](5624-distributed-computing-and-load-balancing.md)'s network-distributed strategies [Parent].
The global volume domain $\Omega$ is partitioned into a grid of chunks.
where $W_x, W_y, W_z$ are the chunk dimensions in voxels [Parent].
Each chunk is treated as an independent unit for loading, processing, or rendering.

To prevent boundary artifacts (e.g., black stripes in compositing or discontinuities in isosurfaces) caused by naive non-overlapping division, a small overlap of data may be included among adjacent datasets [1093-mpi-based-volume-partitioning.md].
These extra/duplicated slices are used for boundary calculations but must be removed before final compositing to prevent image stretching [1093-mpi-based-volume-partitioning.md].
Each unit processes a ray while it traverses its subvolume.
A block is a 3D rectangular slab of adjacent cells.
The concept of partitioning volume data into manageable chunks for parallel processing or out-of-core storage has been fundamental to scalable volume rendering.
Later developments, such as the Moving Walls Algorithm, introduced dynamic partitioning for sparse data on clusters [9715-moving-walls-algorithm.md].

The rise of large-scale scientific datasets (e.g., BigBrain) and interactive applications (e.g., voxel games) has driven the evolution of chunk-based strategies to include neural training [3168-chunk-based-training.md], hierarchical terrain rendering [4050-chunk-trees.md], and residency-aware streaming [10150-tide-trajectory-adaptive-differential-streaming.md].
